trial_name: ELAIN — Early vs Delayed RRT in Enriched KDIGO Stage 2 AKI (2016)
citation: Zarbock A, Kellum JA, Schmidt C, Van Aken H, Wempe C, Pavenstädt H, Boanta A, Gerß J, Meersch M. Effect of Early vs Delayed Initiation of Renal Replacement Therapy on Mortality in Critically Ill Patients With Acute Kidney Injury: The ELAIN Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA. 2016;315(20):2190-2199.
one_liner: In enriched high-risk KDIGO stage 2 AKI, early RRT within 8 hours reduced 90-day mortality compared with delayed initiation (39.3% vs 54.7%, HR 0.66, P=0.03), but subsequent multicentre trials did not confirm benefit.

pico.population: Critically ill adults with KDIGO stage 2 AKI, plasma NGAL >150 ng/mL, plus ≥1 severity criterion (severe sepsis, vasopressors >0.1 μg/kg/min, refractory fluid overload, or non-renal SOFA ≥2)
pico.intervention: Initiate continuous venovenous haemodiafiltration (CVVHDF) within 8 hours of eligibility
pico.comparison: Initiate RRT within 12 hours after KDIGO stage 3 AKI or absolute indications (BUN >100 mg/dL, K+ >6 mEq/L with ECG changes, Mg >8 mEq/L, urine output <200 mL/12 h or anuria, organ oedema)

background.existing_knowledge: Optimal timing of RRT for ICU-associated AKI was uncertain, with wide practice variation. Earlier RRT could improve physiological control but also expose patients to avoidable harms. Prior evidence was heterogeneous.
background.knowledge_gap: Whether early initiation at KDIGO stage 2 with biomarker enrichment reduces mortality.
background.hypothesis: Early RRT within 8 hours of KDIGO stage 2 AKI with NGAL >150 ng/mL and severity criteria reduces 90-day mortality vs delayed initiation.

methods.design: Single-centre, randomised, open-label, parallel-group controlled trial; stratified block randomisation; surgical ICU, Münster, Germany; enrolment Aug 2013–Jun 2015.
methods.setting: Single surgical ICU at a tertiary university hospital.

inclusion: KDIGO stage 2 AKI (creatinine 2.0–2.9× baseline and/or urine output <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥12 h)

Plus ≥1 of: severe sepsis; vasopressors >0.1 μg/kg/min; refractory fluid overload with PaO2/FiO2<300 and/or cumulative fluid balance >10% body weight; development/progression of non-renal organ dysfunction (non-renal SOFA ≥2)
exclusion: AKI due to renal artery occlusion, glomerulonephritis, interstitial nephritis, vasculitis, post-renal obstruction, HUS/TTP
Concurrent participation in another interventional trial

methods.intervention: Initiate CVVHDF within 8 hours of eligibility; effluent target 30 mL/kg/h; pre-dilution replacement; dialysate-to-replacement ratio 1:1; blood flow >110 mL/min; citrate anticoagulation. Stopping criteria: urine output >400 mL/24 h without diuretics (or >2100 mL/24 h with diuretics) plus creatinine clearance >20 mL/min.
methods.comparison: Initiate RRT within 12 hours after KDIGO stage 3 AKI (urine output <0.3 mL/kg/h for ≥24 h and/or ≥3-fold creatinine increase or creatinine ≥4.0 mg/dL with acute rise ≥0.5 mg/dL within 48 h), or within 12 hours if an absolute indication occurred (BUN >100 mg/dL; K+ >6 mEq/L with ECG changes; Mg >8 mEq/L; urine output <200 mL/12 h or anuria; organ oedema in diuretic-resistant AKI).
methods.sample_size_power: 230 patients required to detect an 18% absolute reduction in 90-day mortality (from 55% to 37%) with 80% power at 5% significance; group sequential design with one interim analysis.

headline_bullets: Early RRT reduced 90-day mortality: 39.3% vs 54.7% (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.45–0.97, P=0.03).
Renal recovery at day 90 was higher with early RRT when deaths were included (53.6% vs 38.7%, P=0.02) but similar among survivors (88.2% vs 85.2%, P=0.62).
Mechanical ventilation duration and hospital stay were shorter with early RRT; ICU stay did not differ.

outcomes_table.note: Among those receiving RRT (112 vs 108); absolute difference −18 days (95% CI −41 to 4)

outcomes_table.outcome: Renal recovery at day 90 (deaths counted as no recovery)
Requirement of RRT at day 90 (among survivors with data)
Hospital length of stay (censored at day 90), median (Q1–Q3)
outcomes_table.note: Time-to-discharge analysis with death censoring; absolute difference −37 days

outcomes_table.outcome: ICU length of stay (censored at day 90), median (Q1–Q3)

safety: Serious adverse events (excluding death) among RRT recipients: 1/112 (0.9%) in early group (new-onset arrhythmia) vs 0/108 (0%) in delayed group.

domains.notes: Computer-generated 1:1 stratified block randomisation (block size 10) by cardiovascular SOFA (0–2 vs 3–4) and oliguria. Allocation concealment plausible via computerised assignment.
Open-label design. Mortality is objective, but secondary outcomes (ventilation duration, discharge) are susceptible to performance bias.
No post-randomisation exclusions; full analysis set n=231. Per-protocol analysis pre-specified (112 vs 108 who received RRT).

All early patients received RRT; 108/119 delayed received RRT, 11 avoided RRT entirely. Median time from KDIGO stage 2 to RRT: 6.0 vs 25.5 hours (difference −21.0 h, P<0.001). At initiation, creatinine 1.9 vs 2.4 mg/dL, BUN 38.5 vs 47.5 mg/dL, urine output 445 vs 270 mL (all P≤0.01). Delivered CRRT intensity similar: effluent 26.6 vs 26.6 mL/kg/h, session duration 22.6 vs 22.4 h/day.

Groups broadly similar in severity (SOFA 15.6 vs 16.0, APACHE II 30.6 vs 32.7, ventilated 87.5% vs 88.2%, vasopressors 85.7% vs 90.8%). Some imbalances: men 69.6% vs 57.1%, hypertension 86.6% vs 77.3%, arrhythmia 33.0% vs 44.5%.

internal_validity.verdict: Internal validity is moderate: randomisation and follow-up were robust with a hard primary endpoint, but open-label single-centre design, modest sample size, and baseline imbalances limit confidence beyond mortality.

domains.notes: Predominantly surgical ICU (cardiac/abdominal), very high severity, NGAL enrichment. Excluded eGFR <30. Not representative of general ICU AKI populations.
CVVHDF with citrate anticoagulation; early strategy requires NGAL measurement and severity enrichment, which may not be routine. Single-centre results may not transport to other settings.

external_validity.verdict: External validity is limited to moderate: findings apply to severely ill surgical ICU patients with enriched KDIGO stage 2 AKI managed with continuous RRT in a high-resource setting.

strengths: Randomised evaluation of a hard primary outcome (90-day mortality) in a high-risk cohort.
Clear protocolised contrast with strong separation in timing (median 6.0 vs 25.5 hours from KDIGO stage 2).
Enrichment strategy using NGAL and clinical severity criteria reduced heterogeneity and increased event rates.
Complete inclusion of randomised patients and minimal missingness for the primary outcome.
limitations: Single-centre, open-label design limits generalisability and increases vulnerability to performance bias.
Modest sample size with a large observed effect size increases risk of overestimation and fragility.
Biomarker-driven selection (NGAL threshold) and additional severity criteria constrain applicability.
Several secondary outcomes (ventilation duration, hospital discharge) are highly process-dependent and susceptible to unblinded care.

critical_appraisal.summary: ELAIN provides a signal of mortality benefit with early RRT in an enriched high-risk AKI cohort, but the single-centre open-label design and subsequent discordant multicentre evidence limit confidence and generalisability.
strengths: Hard primary outcome with complete follow-up.
Enrichment strategy increased event rates and biological plausibility.
weaknesses: Modest sample size with large effect size.

sections.authors_conclusion: Early initiation of RRT in critically ill patients with KDIGO stage 2 AKI and elevated NGAL plus severity criteria reduced 90-day mortality compared with delayed initiation.

clinical_bottom_line.verdict: Does not change practice broadly; supports consideration of early RRT only in a highly selected, enriched phenotype similar to the trial, but subsequent evidence favours a more conservative, indication-driven approach.
clinical_bottom_line.applies_to: Severely ill surgical ICU patients with KDIGO stage 2 AKI, NGAL >150 ng/mL, and additional severity criteria, managed with continuous RRT.
clinical_bottom_line.does_not_mean: Early RRT should be routinely initiated at KDIGO stage 2 in all ICU patients; the mortality benefit was not replicated in larger multicentre trials.
implementation_caveats: Requires NGAL measurement and severity enrichment, which may not be routine.
Subsequent trials (STARRT-AKI, IDEAL-ICU) did not show benefit and increased RRT exposure.

controversies.topic: Large effect size despite modest timing separation
controversies.notes: The observed mortality reduction (HR 0.66) with a median separation of only ~19.5 hours raised plausibility concerns, especially for process-dependent secondary outcomes.

controversies.topic: Biomarker-driven enrolment and surgical ICU predominance
controversies.notes: NGAL-based enrichment and predominantly surgical cohort limit transportability to general ICU populations where NGAL testing is not routine.
Correspondence identified ambiguity in adjusted time-to-event modelling; authors clarified the primary HR was unadjusted and corrected the Methods text post-publication.
IDEAL-ICU (septic shock) stopped early for futility; STARRT-AKI showed no survival benefit with accelerated strategy and increased RRT exposure; AKIKI-2 explored even more delayed strategies.

Meta-analyses incorporating ELAIN with larger trials report no consistent mortality benefit from early/accelerated initiation, while early strategies reliably increase RRT use. Guidelines recommend initiating RRT for life-threatening complications, not routinely at earlier KDIGO stages.

context_related_trials.relation: Multicentre RCT in septic shock with severe AKI; stopped early for futility, did not support early RRT.
Large multicentre RCT; no survival benefit with accelerated strategy, increased RRT exposure.
Explored more delayed initiation strategies, informing boundary conditions of 'how late is too late'.

unresolved_questions: What is the optimal trigger for RRT initiation in different AKI phenotypes?
Can biomarker-guided strategies identify patients who benefit from early RRT?
How to balance avoidance of unnecessary RRT with potential benefits of early solute/fluid control?

numbers_to_remember: Renal recovery day 90: 53.6% vs 38.7% (P=0.02) but similar among survivors
quick_recall.one_line_takeaway: In enriched high-risk KDIGO stage 2 AKI, early RRT reduced mortality in a single-centre trial, but subsequent multicentre evidence does not support routine early initiation.
